prompt: The picture below shows the museum's plant in 1998 and after some changes were made in 2008.
essay:
The maps illustrate the changes made to the layout of a museum between 1998 and 2008.

Overall, the museum underwent a substantial reconfiguration over the ten-year period, with the internal arrangement of several facilities being considerably altered and a number of new amenities being incorporated. Despite these extensive modifications, however, the café and the ticket entrance and exit remained broadly unchanged in terms of their location.

In 1998, a centrally positioned garden constituted the principal feature of the museum’s layout, with the café situated immediately behind it. The permanent exhibition rooms occupied the two opposing corners at the ends of the garden. Along the lower section of the premises, a ticket office was positioned adjacent to a shop, a temporary exhibition room, a toilet and a designated area for storing bags. Collectively, these facilities occupied much of the space along the southern edge of the museum.

By 2008, the original configuration had been substantially transformed. The central garden was retained but was enhanced with additional amenities, most notably fountains and a designated café seating area. The permanent exhibition rooms continued to occupy the right-hand side of the premises, effectively retaining their position along the eastern edge, whereas the exhibition facility on the left-hand side was removed altogether. The space formerly occupied by the temporary exhibition room was subsequently repurposed to accommodate the shop and the bag-and-coat storage facilities. Elsewhere, the WC was relocated to a position immediately adjacent to the café, while the temporary exhibition room itself was transferred to the western side of the garden. In addition, a restaurant was introduced in the upper corner of the museum, representing one of the most notable additions to the revised layout.
